cards.text: Last night the council condemned Jesus as deserving of death (Mark 14:64). Now it's early morning, and the chief priests, elders, scribes and the whole Sanhedrin devise a plan. They bind Jesus, lead Him away and hand Him over to Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea (Luke 3:1).

cards.question: Pilate asks Jesus, “Are You the King of the Jews?” What does Jesus say back to him?

cards.text: Then the chief priests start accusing Jesus of many things, and I mean MANY. These folks didn't show up with a charge, friend, they showed up with a whole stack.
So Pilate questions Him again: “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!” Pilate's basically pointing at the pile.

cards.question: Jesus makes no further reply to Pilate. How does Pilate react?

cards.text: Now Pilate has a custom at the feast: one prisoner gets released. A real-life get-out-of-jail-free card.

cards.question: At the feast, the prisoner Pilate releases is the one chosen by ___.

cards.text: Now meet a man named Barabbas, sitting in prison. Friend, look at the company he keeps: the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.

cards.question: The crowd goes up to Pilate during the feast. What do they start asking him to do?

cards.text: So Pilate puts one name right on the table: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?”

cards.question: Pilate knows why the chief priests handed Jesus over to him. They did it out of ___.
But the chief priests stir up the crowd. Who do they want Pilate to release instead of Jesus?

cards.text: So Pilate asks again: “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?” Same crowd, same governor, question number two.

cards.question: Pilate asks the crowd what to do with Jesus. What do they shout back?
True or false: When Pilate asks the crowd, “What evil has He done?” they go quiet.

cards.text: Pilate's asking for a reason. The crowd? They just get LOUDER: “Crucify Him!”

cards.question: True or false: Pilate releases Barabbas because he wants to satisfy the crowd.

cards.text: Barabbas walks out the door a free man. Pilate asked what evil Jesus had done, and now he has Him flogged and hands Him over to be crucified.
Then the soldiers lead Jesus away into the palace, the Praetorium, and call the whole company together. Not a couple of guys, friend, the WHOLE company.

cards.question: The soldiers dress Jesus in a purple robe. Then they make something and set it on His head. What is it?
Robe on, crown on. Now the soldiers begin to salute Jesus. What do they call out?

cards.text: They keep striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they kneel down and bow before Him, and friend, read that one slow.

cards.question: True or false: When the soldiers finish mocking Jesus, they leave the purple robe on Him.

cards.text: They put His own clothes back on Him and lead Him out to crucify Him. We'll stop here for now, friend, but this story is far from over.

findings.problem: Card 6 says only that Pilate's custom releases one prisoner. Nothing in the earlier cards indicates who chooses the prisoner, so the baker must guess the unseen words "the people" rather than reason out the blank.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Pilate's offer in card 10 does not give the baker any basis for identifying the chief priests' motive. The baker can only guess the unseen word "envy," not reason it out from the earlier cards.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
